subject.title: feat(skills): declarative cron-trigger metadata in SKILL.md frontmatter

question: Should OpenClaw accept SKILL.md-declared scheduled/event triggers that can lead to autonomous execution, and if so must they compile through a permissioned routines/cron contract?
rationale: This choice defines a public skill metadata contract and a security boundary for installed content requesting future agent runs, which cannot be safely inferred from current code alone.

options.title: Defer Runtime Execution Until Routines Boundary Lands
options.body: Keep the issue open but do not implement automatic SKILL.md-trigger execution until the durable routines and approval/provenance model are accepted.

options.title: Accept Permissioned Skill Trigger Metadata
options.body: Allow SKILL.md trigger metadata only when it compiles to an operator-approved cron/routine record with revocation and audit history.

options.title: Limit To Documentation Or ClawHub Indexing
options.body: Permit non-executing trigger_description-style metadata for audits/search while rejecting automatic runtime registration from installed skill content.

recommendation.title: Defer Runtime Execution Until Routines Boundary Lands
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open but do not implement automatic SKILL.md-trigger execution until the durable routines and approval/provenance model are accepted.

likelyOwner.reason: The overlapping routines issue/PR and cron product boundary history make steipete the best current routing owner for this decision.
